title: Wednesday's boring SaaS, 28 October 2026
dek: Wednesday, 28 October 2026. Three are Stripe-verified, including newer numbers for uhoh and Get Brazil Visa. AODocs, Volie, EmpowerMX, ProSpend, Zamp, and goHappy are self-reported.

companies.name: AODocs
companies.description: Document control on top of Google Workspace: approval workflows, an audit trail, and process control for the files a company cannot lose. Founded in 2012 by Stéphane Donzé. A LinkedIn count from October 2024 says about 95 employees. An earlier note on this site said 250 staff. I am leaving both.
companies.evidence: Company-stated. Stéphane Donzé said on camera that annual revenue was $60M, the company is profitable, and the EBITDA margin is about 10%. The brief dates that figure to December 2026. It is not a payment-processor connection. The 22 October note on this site was about $30M of revenue for 2026, 15% growth, a 10% profit margin for 2025, and 250 staff.
companies.indieAngle: The control layer on the office suite a regulated company already pays for.
companies.whyItPrints: The company already lives in Drive. Drive does not give them the control an auditor asks for. Once the contracts and the procedures sit in the workflow, leaving means rewriting the process.

companies.name: Volie
companies.description: A contact center for the business-development desk at a car dealership: calls, email, and SMS, matched to the dealer's data. It replaces the desk phone. Founded in 2017. Scott Davis is president and co-founder. Bootstrapped, as told on camera.
companies.evidence: Company-stated, and calculated by Latka from what Scott Davis said on camera. Not a payment-processor connection. About $14.4M revenue for 2026. About a $9.6M run rate for 2024. About 2,000 rooftops. About 63 employees in 2026. About a 16% EBITDA margin. About $1,000 of revenue per rooftop.
companies.indieAngle: One kind of franchise, priced per location, for the outbound desk they already staff.
companies.whyItPrints: A dealership desk lives on outbound calls and the data in the dealer system. A tool that already knows that workflow sticks harder than a generic phone system.

companies.name: EmpowerMX
companies.description: Software for aircraft maintenance, repair, and overhaul. It replaces the paper job with planning, the work itself, and the compliance file. Founded in 1999 by Dinakara Nagalla. Sold to IFS. The acquisition was announced in July 2024.
companies.evidence: Company-stated, Practical Founders, April 2026. No single revenue total in the source, so I am not writing one. He describes a mid-double-digit SaaS business. Contracts from the hundreds of thousands to several million dollars a year. Extremely profitable in the year of the sale. Customers often saw more than 10% savings on maintenance operations. Started at about 12 people. Later growth equity. Sold to IFS from a position he calls strength. Latka estimates were ignored.
companies.indieAngle: Paper to a screen in a trade where the cost of downtime is the sale.
companies.whyItPrints: An airline cannot shrug at a compliance gap. The contracts run for years. He says customers also saw savings on the maintenance work itself.

companies.name: ProSpend
companies.description: Spend management for a mid-market finance team: expenses, bills, purchase orders, budgets, virtual cards, and payments. Bootstrapped in Australia by Sharon Nouh. Sold in 2025 to ISH, a UK software group, so she could expand in the UK with a local partner and still run the product.
companies.evidence: Company-stated, Practical Founders, May 2026. No revenue total in the source. About 1,000 customers and 50 employees. Annual contracts roughly $15,000 to $40,000. Bootstrapped for about 10 years, then a strategic sale, not a distress exit.
companies.indieAngle: Expenses, bills, and cards in one product, sold through the accountants who already have the client.
companies.whyItPrints: A mid-size finance team hates the expense pile and does not want an enterprise suite. The contract size in the article is the mid-market, not a seat at a few dollars.

companies.name: Zamp
companies.description: Sales-tax compliance, sold through accounting firms as a "powered by" product. Founded in 2022 by Rohit Bhadange. This one raised venture money. It is not a bootstrap story.
companies.evidence: Company-stated, from a Latka interview in May 2026. $5M annual revenue by the first quarter of 2025. It was $1M in 2023. About $10,000 of revenue per user. Raised $30M in total, including a $16.5M Series A in October 2025. About 51 employees as of June 2026.
companies.indieAngle: The channel is the accountant who already bills the client every month.
companies.whyItPrints: Sales tax is paperwork an accountant already owns the relationship for. The firm brings the client. The note is the channel, and also that they raised to build it.

companies.name: goHappy
companies.description: Messages and engagement for companies with 1,000 or more hourly workers: restaurants, logistics, manufacturing, retail. It started as an app. Workers would not install it, so it moved to SMS. Shawn Boyer founded it. He also founded Snagajob.
companies.evidence: Company-stated, Practical Founders, October 2026. Revenue well into eight figures. He does not give a tighter number, so I am not writing one. About 1.5 million frontline employees across about 400 customers. A team under 40. Profitable, with solid gross margins. Minority growth equity from Growth Street Partners in 2022, then a majority deal with Pamlico Capital in 2025.
companies.indieAngle: Text the worker. Do not ask them to download the HR app.
companies.whyItPrints: An hourly worker will not install another app. The text message is the channel. The HR system integration is why the employer stays.

companies.name: uhoh.com
companies.description: Flat-fee managed IT help desk / MSP for growing startups — "priced by you," free to try, subscriptions starting ~$3k/mo (up to ~50 staff). Canada-founded, mid-2025.
companies.evidence: MRR $47,157, 37 subscriptions, last-30-day subscription growth +29.7%. Last 30 days $47,350 (up 63.3%). All-time $459,275. Revenue synced 28 October 2026 ~04:21 Warsaw. The 2 October note was about $36,400 a month, 30 subscriptions, about $32,800 in the last 30 days, and about $417,000 all-time.
companies.indieAngle: A desk with a public price and a cap on the team size.
companies.whyItPrints: Selling outsourced IT ops as a productized MSP with transparent Stripe billing. Tiny sub count (30) × high ACV = real print; classic boring B2B services wrapped as SaaS-ish recurring.

companies.name: Fidelatoo
companies.description: Digital loyalty cards for local shops and franchises, so the stamp card is a person instead of a piece of plastic. Founded in 2023. The company says it is in more than 25 countries and has about 1,450 users. A one-line note on 1 October was the first time it showed up here. This is the full write-up.
companies.evidence: MRR $6,898, 244 subscriptions. Last 30 days $7,801 (up 5.3%). Last 12 months $95,304. All-time $171,877. Last-30-day margin about 60% claimed. Revenue synced 28 October 2026 ~11:02 Warsaw. The 1 October one-line note was about $6,900 a month and 239 subscriptions.
companies.indieAngle: A stamp card for one local shop, sold to the owner or to the franchise office.
companies.whyItPrints: A café still has a paper stamp card. Once the points live in the app, the shop keeps paying for the seat.

companies.name: Get Brazil Visa
companies.description: A specialist desk for foreigners applying for Brazilian residency / digital-nomad / retirement / family / investor visas. It helps navigate government portals; every application is personally reviewed by a licensed Brazilian immigration lawyer; 95%+ approval rate claimed (company-stated). Pricing: $599 flat for nomad / retirement / family; investor cases quoted. Founded Dec 2025, BR. React + Cloudflare + Supabase + Stripe. Channels: SEO, content marketing. ~127k Google Search impressions in L30 (TrustMRR / GSC).
companies.evidence: Last 30 days $4,680 (up 180.6%). Last 12 months and all-time $19,153. Last-30-day margin about 95% claimed. About 1,350 visitors in the last 30 days. The subscription line is not the business. People pay for the application. Revenue synced 28 October 2026 ~06:24 Warsaw. The 9 October note was about $3,067 in the last 30 days and about $16,372 all-time.
companies.indieAngle: One country's paperwork, a lawyer on the file, and the search traffic.
companies.whyItPrints: Government portals are hostile; people pay once to have a human + checklist get them through. 95% margin, no seats, SEO-led. Same Conductor pattern as Fast Corp (BG company formation) and Easy Moving Permits (city curb permits).
